notes: Opens mid-turn: the first paragraph, "Y en el párrafo siguiente...", has no label. Checking the full sitting file confirms it is the tail of a Sr. BERHONGARAY.- turn that began before the fragment, so it is not listed as a start. The fragment holds 20 bold speaker labels plus one stray empty bold run (" " inside the president's sentence "del artículo 1° y dije"), which is a WordPerfect artifact and not a label. TWO of those 20 labels are NOT listed as starts, because of rule 2: in both cases the president is the speaker immediately before a stenographer's note and the same president resumes after it, with the label reprinted. They are (a) "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-" / "Reitero: está muy claro que la aprobación del artículo 1 implica la aprobación de todo el anexo.", right after "-Varios señores senadores hablan a la vez."; and (b) "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-" / "Queda definitivamente sancionado el proyecto de ley. Se harán las comunicaciones correspondientes.", right after the run of three notes on articles 2, 3 and 4. This is the one genuinely two-way reading in this stretch. Rule 2 says a note does not start a new turn and that you do not list the same person again; rule 5 says never drop a turn. I followed rule 2 literally, and record both suppressed labels here verbatim so a maintainer who meant the other reading can add them back and get 20 starts instead of 18. Note that the surrounding sitting shows this is the house style, not an anomaly: the president's label is routinely reprinted after every italic note. Label typography: the first six labels print as "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-"/"Sr. BERHONGARAY.-" with the dash flush against the closing bold tag; from the seventh on the typist moved the space inside the bold run ("Sr. BERHONGARAY.- "). Since that is trailing whitespace and not visible printed matter, I recorded every label trimmed. No name is ever printed for the chair in this fragment, so the label stays "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-" with no holder, as printed. No headings, no back-links or other furniture, and no inserted document: everything here is floor exchange over the reconsideration of article 1 of the monotributo bill. SETTLED AT 20: the coordinator resolved the two-way reading above against it, on the project's own evidence (TODO.md's convention "a printed label opens a turn; speech resuming after an event stays in the same turn", the PDF gold set's four separate "Sr. Presidente. —" starts across two electronic votes in gold_2004-04-28_p24.json, and the parser's 497 turn_ids for 497 labelled rows): a printed label ALWAYS opens a turn, and rule 2 covers only an UNLABELLED continuation paragraph. Both suppressed labels, (a) and (b), are therefore now listed in their page positions and this file carries 20 starts; the paragraph above is kept as the record of the original reading and is superseded. The exclusion of the stray empty bold run stands.
